name: Hairline lowering surgery

card.summary: Scalp-advancement surgery that moves the hairline down to shorten a tall forehead; published series are mostly in women, and the scar is the central debate.
card.aka: forehead reduction, scalp advancement, hairline advancement
card.note: Published outcome series are mainly in women with stable hairlines; forum users who are men discuss scar visibility and future hair loss as the main concerns.

quick.overview:
Hairline lowering surgery, also called forehead reduction, is a procedure in which an incision is made along the hairline and the scalp is loosened and pulled forward, so the hair-bearing skin sits lower and the forehead looks shorter. It is described in the plastic surgery literature mainly for women with a naturally high hairline, and as part of facial feminization surgery for transgender women.

On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an option for people who feel a large forehead throws off facial proportions. Users compare it with hair transplants and with hairstyling, and a recurring theme is how visible the scar is and whether it suits men, who may go on to lose hair.
quick.mechanism: The surgeon makes an incision at or just in front of the hairline, releases the scalp from the underlying tissue, and advances it forward before closing the wound. Published reports describe different incision designs and ways of anchoring the advanced scalp, including sutures tunnelled through bone. A hair transplant over the scar is sometimes added afterwards to disguise it.
quick.risks: Reported risks include a visible or widened scar, numbness, and the limits on how far the scalp can be advanced. Forum users also raise the concern that surgery on a hairline that is still receding may leave the scar exposed later. Published series are small and mostly retrospective, and mostly involve women, so outcomes in men are less well documented.

lead: Hairline lowering surgery, also called forehead reduction, hairline advancement or scalp advancement, is a cosmetic procedure that shortens the vertical height of the forehead by moving the hair-bearing scalp forward. A surgeon incises along the hairline, frees the scalp from deeper tissue, advances it and closes the wound [4][6][14]. People use it to bring a tall forehead into better proportion with the eyes, midface and lower face, and the effect is visible immediately after the operation rather than building up over months [5][14].

Surgeons have described it chiefly for women with a lifelong high hairline and as one component of facial feminization surgery, where a lower hairline is combined with brow and frontal bone contouring [2][3][5][14]. Reviews describe the best candidates as people with a stable hairline and a mobile scalp, which in practice has meant mostly women [5][6][15].

Published reports are case series and technique descriptions: a retrospective review of 29 women operated on by one surgeon over 20 years, a series of 91 patients with bone-tunnelling suture fixation, a series of 21 patients with an average forehead reduction of about 22 mm, and several reviews [4][8][16][5][15]. Hair transplantation is the main alternative, and the two approaches are often compared [5][7][10][14].

In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for people who attribute a long forehead to hairline position. Users on looksmax.org describe favourable results and concerns about scarring, and many argue it suits women better than men because of male pattern hair loss [11][12][13].

paras: In hairline lowering, the incision is placed along the front hairline, and the scalp is undermined and moved forward so that the hair-bearing skin covers part of the forehead [4][6]. Wikipedia describes the usual setting as an outpatient procedure under local anaesthesia with intravenous sedation, with the new hairline marked beforehand, often in a gently irregular line so it looks natural [14].

The incision is typically trichophytic, meaning it is cut so that hair grows through the scar and helps hide it. The scalp is separated from the skull far back toward the neck, and cutting the galea, the deep fibrous layer, allows it to stretch further. Surgeons may anchor the advanced scalp with sutures or implants to bone, and the wound is closed in two layers with sutures or clips [14]. A series of 91 patients evaluated one anchoring method, bone-tunnelling suture fixation [8].

Scalp laxity is described as the main determinant of how far the hairline can be advanced. Where the scalp is too tight, tissue expanders can be used to increase the possible advancement [14]. The 2013 review in Facial Plastic Surgery Clinics describes the procedure as adapted from scalp reduction and flap techniques [6].

A plastic surgery paper on forehead lifting explains that an incision just in front of the hairline shortens the forehead but does not by itself produce a true hairline advancement, and that standard coronal and endoscopic brow lifts can raise the hairline, one reason surgeons hesitate to recommend them to patients with high hairlines [1].

The procedure grew out of scalp reduction and flap techniques used in hair restoration and reconstructive surgery [6]. A 1999 paper in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery addressed hairline lowering as part of forehead rejuvenation, because surgeons were concerned that standard brow lift techniques worsened a high hairline [1]. A 2009 report in Archives of Facial Plastic Surgery analysed a single surgeon's 20 years of experience with high female hairlines [4].

Its use expanded through facial feminization surgery, in which hairline lowering is one of the steps alongside brow and frontal sinus contouring. A 2012 case report described a 39-year-old transgender woman treated with frontal sinus reshaping, brow lift and hairline lowering [3], and later reviews of forehead contouring and brow bossing reduction describe hairline adjustment as one of the standard upper face techniques [17][18].

Most published series involve women with a naturally high hairline who want a shorter forehead [4][9]. A 2013 review says the operation is best suited to people, typically women, with a lifelong history of a high hairline and no personal or family history of progressive hair loss, and describes very high patient satisfaction [6]. A technique description with outcome analysis in female patients reports measured changes in forehead height [9].

Hairline lowering is among the procedures used in facial feminization surgery, where testosterone-related changes such as an elevated, squared hairline and a projecting brow are treated together [2][3][17]. A review of 220 consecutive patients describes the broader set of operations in this field [2]. A 2023 review of forehead contouring says the upper third of the face has a strong effect on how a face is gendered [18].
Hairline lowering foreheadplasty has also been described alongside tissue expansion in the management of primary cutis verticis gyrata, a scalp condition [21].

Reviews describe the ideal candidate as someone with a stable frontal hairline and a fairly to very mobile scalp, because that combination allows enough advancement to justify an incision across the whole hairline [5][15]. One review says this excludes most men [5]. Wikipedia notes that the scar in men with progressive balding may become more visible over time [14].

Surgeons also consider cultural and ethnic differences in aesthetic ideals, hair characteristics and healing when planning hairline work, and a review of hair restoration in ethnic patients covers shortening an overly high hairline as one of the indications [19].

A retrospective review of 29 women operated on by one surgeon over 20 years reported standardized photograph measurements of the hairline and facial height before and after surgery [4]. A series of 91 patients evaluated hairline lowering with bone-tunnelling suture fixation and reported on its effectiveness and safety [8]. A paper analysed surgical details and outcomes in female patients undergoing aesthetic forehead reduction [9]. A 2025 article describes the surgical anatomy and technique and reports on 21 patients operated between 2019 and 2023, with an average forehead reduction of about 22 mm; its most common complaint was scalp hypoesthesia (reduced sensation) [16].

A 2020 review by surgeons who developed their approach over more than 90 of these operations describes advantages such as immediate results and unsurpassed density, and reports consistent results with low complication rates [5]. A 2026 review in the same journal describes the surgery's steps and likewise lists immediate results and density among its advantages [15].

Hair transplantation has also been studied as an alternative way to lower the frontal hairline, including a series in Asian women with high foreheads [10]; reviews cover transplantation techniques in transgender and gender-diverse patients [7][20]. These reports are largely retrospective and uncontrolled, and none is a randomized trial.

sections.h: Hairline lowering compared with hair transplantation
paras: Wikipedia states that follicular unit hair transplantation can take up to two years to reach comparable density, while the result of hairline lowering is nearly immediate [14]. Surgeon reviews describe hairline lowering as an alternative to transplantation with advantages in density and immediacy, offset by a more invasive operation and a longer scar [5][15].

Transplantation involves no long incision and can be used on hairlines that are still receding, although results on an unstable hairline may change as hair loss continues, a point forum guides emphasise [11]. Transplants are also used after hairline lowering to disguise the scar [13][14].

The scar along the hairline is the most discussed drawback in the surgical and forum discussion. Reviews address scar placement and closure as central to the design [5][6]. Wikipedia says the scar is usually hidden by regrowth but can show with cowlicks, and lists temporary shock loss (thinning) and infection, described as rare, among the risks [14]. The 21-patient series reported scalp numbness as the most common complaint [16].

A user on looksmax.org who describes extensive research argued that scars vary between individuals, can stretch, and may be visible in some lighting or after swimming, and that results shown online may be flattering because of makeup and photography [13]. Another user who had the operation reported a red line during healing that eventually became essentially unnoticeable [12].

Because the operation is mostly described in women, whose hairlines are generally stable, forum commentators argue that in men the possibility of later recession complicates planning; they suggest assessing whether the hairline is stable before any surgical or transplant approach [11][13].

Users on looksmax.org discuss the procedure in guides, personal result threads and cautionary threads. One long guide describes first deciding whether a perceived large forehead comes from the hairline or the proportions of the face, then comparing hairstyling, hair transplants and surgery [11]. Result posts describe the operation as helpful but sometimes costly relative to the change achieved; one poster who posted photos taken two months after surgery said the change was modest and the operation overpriced, while a replier saw a big difference [12]. A critical thread argues that for most men it carries drawbacks that surgeons do not emphasise, while acknowledging it can deliver good results [13]. Other threads discuss cost and low-priced overseas offers, which are mentioned here only as a topic of discussion.

timeline.event: A plastic surgery paper discusses hairline lowering during forehead rejuvenation, noting that standard techniques can raise the hairline [1].
A 20-year single-surgeon review of hairline lowering in 29 women is published [4].
A case report combines hairline lowering with frontal sinus reshaping and brow lift in a transgender woman [3].
A review in Facial Plastic Surgery Clinics describes hairline advancement as adapted from scalp reduction and flap techniques [6].
A series of 91 patients evaluates bone-tunnelling suture fixation [8]; a series in Asian women evaluates hair transplantation to lower the hairline [10].
A review of 220 consecutive facial feminization patients is published [2], and a hairline-lowering review reports a technique developed over more than 90 operations [5].
A study analyses surgical details and outcomes of aesthetic forehead reduction in women [9].
A 21-patient series (2019-2023) reports an average forehead reduction of about 22 mm [16].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, hairline lowering is discussed as a hardmaxxing alternative to hair transplants for a long forehead, with debate centring on the scar and on whether it suits men [11][12][13].

claims.claim: A tall forehead is often a hairline issue that surgery can fix.
claims.believers: A guide author says many people blame face shape for a large forehead, though in most cases the hairline is the cause, and a result thread reports a visible improvement after surgery [11][12].
claims.experts: Surgical series in women report measured reductions in forehead height after hairline lowering [4][9].

claims.claim: The scar makes it a poor choice for most men.
claims.believers: A critical thread says scarring varies, can stretch, and is visible in some conditions, and that before-and-after pictures online are flattered by lighting and makeup [13].
claims.experts: Reviews treat scar placement and closure as a central design issue; published series are mostly in women and report acceptable scars, so male outcomes are less documented [4][5][6].

claims.claim: A hair transplant over the scar can disguise it.
claims.believers: Forum users say transplants over the scar are used, though one says graft placement within scar tissue can be a problem [13].
claims.experts: Reviews of hairline lowering and of transplant techniques discuss combining the two approaches [5][7].

claims.claim: The hairline must be stable before any surgical option.
claims.believers: A guide author says to determine whether the hairline is stable or receding first, since a transplant on an unstable hairline may not look good in a few years [11].
claims.experts: A surgical paper notes the concern that surgery can alter hairline position over time, and series mostly describe women with stable hairlines [1][4].

claims.claim: Women are the better candidates because their hairlines are stable.
claims.believers: Forum commentators say women have no risk of balding, rounder hairlines and can use makeup to hide scars, so the operation works better for them [13].
claims.experts: Surgeon reviews say candidates need a stable hairline and mobile scalp, which they note excludes most men [5][6].

claims.claim: Hairline lowering gives results that hair transplants cannot match for density and speed.
claims.believers: Result posters describe a visible change within months of surgery [12].
claims.experts: Surgeon reviews describe immediate results and dense hair compared with transplantation, which can take up to two years to reach comparable density [5][14].

angle.text: Hairline lowering moves the hair-bearing scalp down so the upper third of the face is shorter. People use it to rebalance facial thirds when a tall forehead is the main feature they want to change, with the result visible straight away [5][14].
